title: One Bed-Hold Reservation per Leave
content:
**Rule (Bed-Hold and Leave Reservations).** A resident may have any number of bed-hold reservations over time, one per leave, but only one that is notice pending or held at a time; a leave that runs straight from one hospital to another is the same hospitalization and the same reservation. A new reservation is opened only when the resident has no other reservation that is notice pending or held.

There is no limit on how many reservations one resident may have over time; the limit is on how many may be open together, and that number is one.

### Condition for opening a reservation

| The resident's other reservations, as the reservation records show them | A new reservation may be opened |
|---|---|
| none is notice pending or held (all are declined, returned, released or expired, or there are none) | Yes |
| one is notice pending or held | No |

The test is made on the system's reservation records for the same resident before the reservation is opened; what decides it is the status those records carry.

### One hospitalization, one reservation

A hospitalization is the continuous absence from the transfer to the return. A resident transferred from the hospital that admitted them straight to a second hospital, without coming back to the center in between, is still on the same hospitalization and therefore on the same reservation; no second reservation is opened for the second hospital.

**Hypothetical sequence.** A resident's spring hospital leave ended with a return and the reservation shows returned. Months later a home visit begins: with no reservation notice pending or held, a new reservation is opened for it. Had the earlier reservation still been held at that moment, no new one could be opened.
